meno.postmenopausal_bleeding.title: Bleeding after menopause
meno.postmenopausal_bleeding.body: Any bleeding or spotting, even a little, 12 months or more after your last period should be checked. Usually the cause is simple, but an early check matters.
meno.postmenopausal_bleeding.seen: You logged bleeding or spotting; the last time on {meno_bleeding_on}.
meno.postmenopausal_bleeding.confidence: This comes from your own log, not a diagnosis; only an exam can tell the cause.

meno.checkup_overdue.title: A checkup is overdue
meno.checkup_overdue.body: {meno_overdue_checkup} is past its due time. Booking it soon keeps your health plan on track.

meno.score_worsened.title: Your symptom score went up
meno.score_worsened.body: Your latest score is {meno_score_total}, {meno_score_rise} points higher than the time before ({meno_score_previous}). Note what changed, and talk to your doctor if it stays high.
meno.score_worsened.seen: Your monthly score went from {meno_score_previous} to {meno_score_total}.
meno.score_worsened.confidence: This comes from the questionnaire you filled in, not a diagnosis.

meno.hrt_review.title: Treatment review coming up
meno.hrt_review.body: The review of {meno_hrt_name} with your doctor ({meno_hrt_on}) is coming up. Write down how you have felt and any side effects to take with you.

meno.checkup_due.title: A checkup is due
meno.checkup_due.body: It is time for {meno_due_checkup}. Regular checks matter more for your bones and heart after menopause.

meno.tip_stage_peri.title: Perimenopause
meno.tip_stage_peri.body: Periods may become irregular, lighter or heavier, and new symptoms may start. Logging periods and symptoms helps you see patterns and talk to your doctor in detail.

meno.tip_stage_meno.title: Menopause
meno.tip_stage_meno.body: It has been more than 12 months, which means you have reached menopause. From now on, log any bleeding or spotting and tell your doctor.

meno.tip_stage_post.title: Postmenopause
meno.tip_stage_post.body: In these years caring for your bones and heart matters more. Keep up with regular checkups and tell your doctor about any bleeding or spotting.

meno.tip_stage_unsure.title: Not sure
meno.tip_stage_unsure.body: If you are not sure where you are, the approximate date of your last period helps. 12 months without a period means menopause; your doctor can tell you more.
